claims.claim: The giant was about ten feet long / a "ten-foot man"
claims.quote: It was a 10-foot-tall (3.0 m), roughly 3,000 pound purported "petrified man"

claims.claim: It was found in a well pit / by men digging a well
claims.quote: uncovered on October 16, 1869, by workers digging a well behind the barn of William C. "Stub" Newell, in Cardiff, New York

claims.claim: The discovery happened at Cardiff, New York, on 16 October 1869
claims.quote: uncovered on October 16, 1869, by workers digging a well behind the barn of William C. "Stub" Newell, in Cardiff, New York

claims.claim: Two hired diggers made the find, behind a barn
claims.quote: Newell hired Gideon Emmons and Henry Nichols, ostensibly to dig a well, and on October 16, 1869, they found the giant.

claims.quote:
Date: 1910

claims.claim: A printed sheet listed the giant's measurements
claims.quote: ITS DIMENSIONS ARE

claims.claim: The figure measured ten feet four and a half inches long
claims.quote: Whole length of the figure, 10 feet, 4½ inches

claims.claim: The nose measured six inches
claims.quote: length of nose, 6 inches

claims.claim: The mouth was four inches wide
claims.quote: width of mouth, 4 inches

claims.claim: The lithograph is by Popular Graphic Arts and is titled "The Onondaga Giant"
claims.quote: THE ONONDAGA GIANT.

claims.claim: The giant began as a block of gypsum
claims.quote: hired men to quarry out a 10-foot-4.5-inch-long (3.2 m) block of gypsum in Fort Dodge, Iowa

claims.claim: The block was quarried at Fort Dodge, Iowa, in 1868
claims.quote: In 1868, Hull, accompanied by a man named H. B. Martin, hired men to quarry out a 10-foot-4.5-inch-long (3.2 m) block of gypsum in Fort Dodge, Iowa

claims.claim: The quarry workmen were told the block was for a Lincoln monument
claims.quote: telling them it was intended for a monument to Abraham Lincoln in New York

claims.claim: The stereocard views date from 1873 and show Cardiff Glen near Fort Dodge, Iowa
claims.quote: VIEW IN CARDIFF GLEN. NEAR FORT DODGE.IOWA.

claims.claim: Whether the Chicago stonecutter knew what he was carving is unresolved
claims.quote: While it is not clear if Burkhardt was aware of Hull's intentions, it is reported that they took steps to cover up their work during the carving

claims.claim: The Chicago stonecutter who took the job was Edward Burkhardt
claims.quote: He shipped the block to Edward Burkhardt in Chicago, a German stonecutter.

claims.claim: Hull confessed on 10 December 1869
claims.quote: On December 10, 1869, Hull confessed everything to the press

claims.claim: Both giants were ruled fakes in court in February 1870
claims.quote: on February 2, 1870, both giants were revealed as fakes in court

claims.claim: Newell covered the find with a tent and charged fifty cents for a fifteen-minute viewing
claims.quote: a tent was set up on the discovery site and Newell charged each visitor fifty cents for a fifteen-minute session of viewing the giant

claims.claim: Three to five hundred people came per day
claims.quote: The number of visitors went to about three to five hundred per day

claims.claim: George Hull was Newell's cousin and a tobacconist
claims.quote: During November 1868, Hull transported the giant by railroad to the farm of his cousin, William Newell.

claims.claim: Hull lost an argument with a preacher about the giants named in Genesis
claims.quote: Hull got into an argument with Reverend Turk and his supporters at a Methodist revival meeting about Genesis 6:4, which states that there were giants who once lived on Earth. Hull, a skeptic, being the minority party, lost the argument.

claims.claim: The giant was carved in Chicago in Hull's own likeness
claims.quote: The giant was designed to imitate the form of Hull himself.

claims.claim: Sand, sulphuric acid and a board of steel knitting needles were used to age the surface and simulate pores
claims.quote: Hull first wiped the giant using a sponge soaked with sand and water. The giant's surface was beaten with steel knitting needles embedded in a board to simulate pores. The giant was also rubbed with sulphuric acid to create a deeper, vintage-like color.

claims.claim: The hoax cost $2,600 in total
claims.quote: By then, he had spent US$2,600 (equivalent to $63,000 in 2025) for the hoax.

claims.claim: Geologists quickly recognised it was not a petrified man
claims.quote: John F. Boynton, the first geologist to examine the giant, declared that it could not be a fossilized man

claims.claim: Yale's Othniel Marsh called it "a most decided humbug"
claims.quote: Yale paleontologist Othniel C. Marsh examined the statue ... and termed it "a most decided humbug"

claims.claim: Marsh's reasoning was that soluble gypsum buried for centuries would not still carry fresh tool marks
claims.quote: pointing out that it was made of soluble gypsum, which, had it been buried in its blanket of wet earth for centuries, would not still have fresh tool marks on it (which it did)

claims.claim: P. T. Barnum's copy was a plaster copy
claims.quote: he hired a man to model the giant's shape covertly in wax and create a plaster copy

claims.claim: A Michigan arcade owner says the copy displayed there is Barnum's
claims.quote: The owner of Marvin's Marvelous Mechanical Museum, a coin-operated game arcade and museum of oddities in Farmington Hills, Michigan, has said that the copy displayed there is Barnum's.
